submissions.suggestedProjectName: xAI Colossus 2 (existing tracked project — could not confirm DB id, API unreachable)
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: legal/regulatory risk update for tracked project 'xAI Colossus 2' (Memphis/Southaven). NAACP v. xAI Corp / MZX Tech (N.D. Miss.), a Clean Air Act suit over unpermitted gas turbines powering this site, has a federal court evidentiary hearing on the NAACP's preliminary-injunction motion scheduled for TODAY, Aug 24, 2026 (per Earthjustice's case tracking page and contemporaneous coverage of the docket) — outcome not yet public as of this submission and could not be confirmed via available search. DOJ intervened in June 2026 seeking dismissal on national-security grounds; Mississippi's Permit Board separately approved 41 of the turbines in March 2026, leaving the remaining ~18 (or 59 total per this source, which conflicts with other counts — figures are inconsistent across coverage and should be verified) unpermitted. A shutdown order would directly affect this project's operational status. Recommend flagging for a follow-up check once the hearing outcome is reported.

submissions.title: Texas will audit up to 300 projects, mostly data centers, after Gov. Greg Abbott's order
submissions.excerpt: Texas will audit up to 300 projects, mostly data centers, after Gov. Greg Abbott's order
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION (statewide, no single project — reviewer may want a standalone restriction record rather than a per-project one): Gov. Abbott directed the PUC and ERCOT on Aug 3, 2026 to audit every data center project in ERCOT's interconnection queue (~250-300 projects, reportedly accounting for >200GW of requested future demand — more than twice ERCOT's peak-demand record) before any can connect to the grid; ERCOT says the audit will take 'several months.' This is a de facto statewide pause on new Texas data-center grid connections and is directly relevant to most of this tracker's ~20+ Texas-sited projects (Stargate Shackelford/Milam/Wisconsin/Doña Ana County, Meta El Paso, Crusoe Goodnight, IREN Childress/Sweetwater, Cipher Black Pearl, Aligned Caprock, and others). Governor's quote (gov.texas.gov): projects that fail to comply 'must be denied connection to the Texas grid.'

submissions.title: Inside Amazon's nearly 3,000-acre data center project outside of Houston
submissions.excerpt: Inside Amazon's nearly 3,000-acre data center project outside of Houston
submissions.note: New AWS/Amazon project, not currently in the tracker. 'Project Eagle': up to 10-building campus on ~3,000 acres near Boling, Wharton County, TX, ~60 miles SE of Houston. Total investment reported as ~$10B across multiple outlets (an initial-phase permit was filed at ~$1.2B per usdatacenterprojects.com, so treat $10B as an aggregate/eventual figure, not a confirmed capex disclosure). Peak power reported as 'up to 75 MW' — this looks low for a $10B/10-building campus and may reflect only an early construction-phase load rather than eventual IT or site capacity; flagging for reviewer verification rather than treating as final. The project is also subject to Gov. Abbott's statewide ERCOT/PUCT interconnection audit (see companion siting-restriction submission) and has not secured a grid connection as of mid-Aug 2026. Publication date is an estimate; exact date not confirmed (network egress to fetch full article was blocked).

claims.methodology: Aggregate project cost as reported across multiple news outlets citing county officials/permit filings; not a company-disclosed figure.
'Up to 75 MW at peak' as reported by Houston Chronicle and other outlets; basis (IT load vs. site power) unclear, and the figure may be incomplete for the project's eventual scale.

submissions.title: OpenAI Unveils 3.2GW 'Project Camellia' Data Center Campus in Effingham County, Georgia
submissions.excerpt: OpenAI Unveils 3.2GW 'Project Camellia' Data Center Campus in Effingham County, Georgia
submissions.note: New OpenAI project, not currently in the tracker. 3.2GW campus (4 buildings, Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub, ~2,600 acres) near Rincon, GA; Georgia Power to deliver power in phases from 2028 to 2032. Cost reported as ~$20B initially, with an OpenAI VP quoted (per CBS Atlanta) estimating >$30B at full build-out — treat as a range, not a single confirmed capex figure. OpenAI states it will fund all infrastructure/electric-service costs itself (no ratepayer subsidy claimed) and receives a 50% property-tax abatement for 15 years. Primary source is OpenAI's own announcement at openai.com/index/building-ai-infrastructure-with-the-effingham-county-community/ — not independently fetched due to sandboxed network access, so the excerpt above is drawn from secondary trade-press coverage instead; figures are corroborated across multiple outlets (DCD, CBS Atlanta, Effingham Herald, county government site).

claims.methodology: 3.2GW figure as reported in secondary coverage of the company's own announcement; phased delivery 2028-2032; basis (site power vs. IT load) not independently confirmed.

submissions.title: Meta to build $13 billion Alberta data centre, its first in Canada
submissions.excerpt: Meta to build $13 billion Alberta data centre, its first in Canada
submissions.note: New Meta project, not currently in the tracker (distinct from the already-tracked 'Wonder Valley Phase 1' in Alberta, which is owned by O'Leary Ventures, not Meta). Meta's first Canadian data center: Sturgeon County, Alberta; 1GW initial capacity, scalable to 1.8GW; C$13B (~US$9.17B at reporting-date FX) total investment; ~3,000 peak construction workers, 300+ permanent jobs. Meta says it will fully fund new generation/grid infrastructure and match consumption with 100% clean/renewable energy, but has also partnered with Pembina Pipeline to build a new gas-fired 'Greenlight Electricity Centre' in Sturgeon County (in service late 2030) as the actual generation source — worth flagging for the power-source/siting field, since the renewable-matching claim and the underlying gas-fired generation are two different things.

claims.methodology: Company-stated 1GW initial capacity, scalable to 1.8GW, per secondary coverage of Meta's announcement; basis not fully specified.
C$13B converted to USD (~$9.17B) as reported by outlets; not independently verified against a primary USD figure from Meta.
